## Objective
- Complete a playable mobile-friendly platformer RPG about reaching agreements through personality-based conversations.
- Keep Mira visually aligned with the ground characters and preserve the steampunk/magical ambience.

## Requirements
- 2D game for phone/tablet with platforming, turn-based conversations, and touch controls.
- Character abilities should reflect traits such as charisma and empathy.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas game with keyboard and touch input.
- Mira is a mediator in Windmere, wearing a teal-and-brass travel outfit, goggles, and a top hat.
- The setting uses a dusky village scene with brass gears, a drifting airship, and magical floating motes.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game UI, welcome/help/ending screens, dialogue layout, responsive controls, Canvas scenery, characters, platforms, and keepsakes.
- Added conversation actions, trait-based trust gains, agreement completion, HUD updates, ending/replay, help and sound toggles, keyboard and pointer handlers.
- Fixed a missing closing brace in `drawProps()` after `node --check game.js` reported `Unexpected token 'function'`.

### Active
- Validate the latest `game.js` syntax and test the complete game loop in a browser, including mobile controls.
- Inspect a current screenshot and fix any runtime or visual issues.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Run `node --check game.js` again; a closing `})();` was added after the last syntax check, which had reported `Unexpected end of input`.
2. Run the game in a browser and verify the opening screen, movement, jumping, conversations, agreement completion, replay, and touch controls.
3. Capture and inspect a screenshot; address any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Canvas rendering, game state, conversations, input handlers, and UI wiring.
- `index.html`: Game UI and screen structure.
- `style.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Three NPCs have distinct preferred conversation actions; agreements require trust and an explicit “Seal the agreement” action.

## Objective
- Complete a playable, mobile-friendly platformer RPG about reaching agreements through personality-based conversations.

- 2D game for phone/tablet with platforming, turn-based conversations, and touch controls.

- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas game with keyboard and touch input.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, battle system, and new creature drawing function.
- `index.html`: Game screens and newly added battle interface.
- `style.css`: Existing responsive styling; battle UI styles still need implementation.

## Objective
- Complete a playable, mobile-friendly platformer RPG about reaching agreements through personality-based conversations, with party battles and varied fantasy-creature NPCs.

## Requirements
- 2D game for phone/tablet with platforming, turn-based conversations, and touch controls.
- Character abilities reflect traits such as charisma and empathy.
- NPCs are grounded fantasy creatures with varied appearances and equipment.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas game with keyboard and touch input.
- Keep Mira as mediator in Windmere, wearing a teal-and-brass travel outfit, goggles, and a top hat.
- Preserve the dusky village scenery and explicit “Seal the agreement” action.
- Add menu-driven party battles alongside platforming and conversations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Responsive platforming, three personality-based conversations, agreement completion, HUD, ending/replay, and help/sound toggles are implemented.
- Battle UI markup, two encounters, party stats, turn-based Attack/Magic/Guard actions, enemy turns, recovery, victory handling, and replay reset logic are implemented.
- Added distinct creature designs for Lena, Bo, and Sol; `drawWorld` now calls `drawNeighbor`.
- `node --check game.js` passes after the NPC drawing-call change.

### Active
- Add responsive battle-screen styles in `style.css`; current CSS has no battle-specific selectors.
- Validate encounters, party commands, victory/recovery, replay, all conversations, and mobile layouts.
- Update help text to explain battles.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement desktop and mobile styles for `.battle-screen` and its child elements in `style.css`.
2. Update help text in `index.html` to mention encounters and party commands.
3. Test battle and conversation flows, mobile layouts, and replay; check whether player movement should be disabled while a battle is active.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, battle system, and creature drawing.
- `index.html`: Game screens, battle interface, and help text.
- `style.css`: Responsive styling; battle-screen styles are missing.

## Important Context
- Earlier browser testing completed all three conversations and agreements, reaching the ending with `3 of 3 agreements` and 6 thoughtful turns.
- Repository files currently appear untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, and other existing project files); no commit state was reported.

## Objective
- Expand the existing playable platformer RPG into a tiny-world fantasy adventure about overthrowing seven dictators, while retaining its mobile-friendly platforming and turn-based party battles.
- Give each country eight distinct combatant types before its final boss, with varied steampunk-and-magic aesthetics.

## Requirements
- The world should feel tiny, on a scale comparable to an ant’s perspective.
- Seven distinct countries, each with eight combatant types leading to a final boss.
- Steampunk-meets-magic setting with varied designs and non-repeating patterns.
- Preserve the existing game’s mobile-friendly platforming, touch controls, personality-based conversations, and party battles.

## Decisions
- Keep the existing self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas game structure.
- Represent seven countries and their rosters as data-driven content in `game.js`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing Windmere platforming, conversations, agreement ending/replay, touch controls, and two turn-based encounters are implemented.
- Added a seven-country data structure in `game.js`, with named tyrants/bosses and eight uniquely named, themed combatants per country; generated encounters are arranged across a larger world map.
- `game.js` now derives world width from the seven regions.

### Active
- Integrate the new country progression with gameplay and UI: country-specific scenery/labels, region-appropriate encounter appearances, and boss progression.
- Review existing assumptions tied to three agreements and two encounters; update ending, HUD, reset, encounter gating, and help text to fit the expanded storyline.
- Validate the complete journey and mobile layouts in a browser.

- (none)

1. Inspect and update `game.js` rendering and encounter progression so the seven countries feel distinct and final bosses follow each set of eight combatants.

3. Run syntax and diff checks, then browser-test battles, conversations, campaign progression, replay, and mobile layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Existing game systems plus newly added country and encounter data.
- `index.html`: Game screens, HUD, battle UI, intro, ending, and help copy.
- `style.css`: Responsive game, battle, and overlay presentation.

## Important Context
- The new `countries` array and generated `encounters` are in `game.js`; each region currently has nine generated encounters (eight foes plus boss), positioned across a 14,700-unit world.
- Existing storyline logic still ends at three agreements, and the ending/help/UI still describe Windmere and two encounters; these are not yet reconciled with the new campaign.

## Objective
- Expand the platformer RPG into a tiny-world steampunk fantasy adventure across seven countries, overthrowing their dictators while retaining conversations, party battles, and mobile-friendly controls.

## Requirements
- Seven distinct countries, each with eight combatant types before its final boss.
- Preserve platforming, touch controls, personality-based conversations, and turn-based party battles.
- Keep the self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas structure; store country and encounter content in `game.js`.

## Decisions
- Country and encounter content is data-driven in `game.js`.
- Combat encounters progress sequentially, with tyrant defeat tracking the campaign’s seven-country completion.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added seven countries, eight themed combatants per country, and one boss per country in a 14,700-unit world.
- Updated campaign copy, HUD labels, country-specific scenery, encounter highlighting, sequential gating, and completion after all seven tyrants are defeated.
- Updated battle continuation to refresh HUD progress and show the ending after the final boss.
- Confirmed `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Validate battles and sequential progression through all 63 encounters, conversations, ending, replay/reset, and desktop/mobile layouts.
- Review Windmere-specific NPCs and keepsakes for consistency with the seven-country campaign.

- (none)

1. Browser-test campaign flow, battle progression, completion, replay/reset, and responsive/mobile controls.
2. Review and resolve the Windmere-specific NPCs and keepsakes in `game.js`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Country and encounter data, NPCs, keepsakes, campaign progression, rendering, battles, conversations, and reset logic.
- `index.html`: Campaign UI, HUD labels, dialogue, battle, ending, and help copy.
- `style.css`: Responsive and mobile presentation.

- Project files are untracked according to `git status --short --branch`; no commit or push was made.
- `npcData` and `keepsakes` remain Windmere-specific; only three NPCs and three keepsakes are currently defined.
- Browser testing has not yet been performed.

- Expand the platformer RPG into a tiny-world steampunk fantasy adventure across seven countries, overthrowing their dictators while retaining conversations, party battles, and mobile-friendly controls.

## Requirements
- Seven distinct countries, each with eight combatant types before its final boss.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

- default:
  - status: open
  - browser-type: chromium
  - user-data-dir: <in-memory>
  - headed: true
